pr_title: Change `Target` from a `CodeProperty` to be an `AliasProperty` that points to `FileSystemInfo.LinkTarget`
pr_body:
<!-- Anything that looks like this is a comment and can't be seen after the Pull Request is created. -->

# PR Summary

Fix #15958
Fix #13365

Change `Target` from a `CodeProperty` to be an `AliasProperty` that points to `FileSystemInfo.LinkTarget`.
Also, keep the public API `InternalSymbolicLinkLinkCodeMethods.GetTarget(PSObject instance)`, but use `FileSystemInfo.LinkTarget` inside.

I have reviewed the .NET implementation of `LinkTarget`, and can confirm that the functionality is in parity.
The only difference is that `LinkTarget` doesn't throw error when the file doesn't exist, but our `GetTarget(...)` throws exception in that case. So, I add the file-existence check at some places, and other places doesn't need the check.

It would be easier to review by ignoring the white-space changes:
https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/pull/16165/files?w=1

issue_context.title: FileSystemProvider.NameString uses realpath in Linux which resolves all links while Windows just returns the next target
issue_context.body:
### Prerequisites

- [X] Write a descriptive title.
- [X] Make sure you are able to repro it on the [latest released version](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/releases)
- [X] Search the existing issues.
- [X] Refer to the [FAQ](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/master/docs/FAQ.md).
- [X] Refer to [Differences between Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell](https://docs.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/whats-new/differences-from-windows-powershell).

### Steps to reproduce

Create 2 links and 1 file:
```bash
touch foo
ln -s bar foo
ln -s baz bar
```

so you have baz -> bar -> foo

I used the following Cmdlet to exemplify the error:
```cs
using System.Management.Automation;  // Windows PowerShell assembly.
using Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands;

namespace SendGreeting
{
  [Cmdlet(VerbsCommunications.Send, "Greeting")]
  public class SendGreetingCommand : Cmdlet
  {
    protected override void ProcessRecord()
    {
      WriteObject("Hello " + name + "!!");
      string fileName = FileSystemProvider.NameString(new PSObject(new System.IO.FileInfo("/home/user/baz")));
      WriteObject(fileName);
    }
  }
}
```
```pwsh
Import-Module /home/user/Cmdlet/bin/Debug/net5.0/Cmdlet.dll
Send-Greeting
```

### Expected behavior

```console
baz -> bar
```


### Actual behavior

```console
baz -> foo
```


### Error details
This differs with Windows and also seems to differ when realpath fails since it fallsback to readlink:
https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell-Native/blob/deb01d6f65b07a0861933a2986cce2318fd60492/src/libpsl-native/src/followsymlink.cpp#L39-L54

### Environment data

```powershell
PS /home/jozky/pscore> $PSVersionTable

Name                           Value
----                           -----
PSVersion                      7.1.4
PSEdition                      Core
GitCommitId                    7.1.4
OS                             Linux 4.19.128-microsoft-standard #1 SMP Tue Jun 23 12:58:10 UTC 2020
Platform                       Unix
PSCompatibleVersions           {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0…}
PSRemotingProtocolVersion      2.3
SerializationVersion           1.1.0.1
WSManStackVersion              3.0
```


### Visuals

_No response_
comments: The ` FileSystemProvider.NameString()` is used in Formatting subsystem primary in `dir` scenario where users investigate full path chain step-by-step. So it is a bug (and a minor breaking change).

WG discussed this and agree that the behavior is a little surprising - as far as we can tell there aren't any other *nix tools (like ls, readlink, stat) that behave this way. It's unknown if PowerShell has internal code that rely on the current behavior. This _is_ a breaking change as the API results may be different, so anyone relying on previous results may be affected.

:tada:This issue was addressed in #16165, which has now been successfully released as `v7.2.0-rc.1`.:tada:

review_comments: Add the file-existence check here, to keep the existing behavior.
I'd accept the breaking change as unlikely breaking change. It is more native and convince as discussed at LinkTarget design time. I suggest to weight this.

Do you mean that you think this check is not needed?
The `GetTarget` public method is kept only for back-compat purpose. It's not used by PowerShell code directly. So, I think it makes more sense to keep the same behavior as before.
Ok, in the case should we add Obsolete attribute?
Yeah, that sounds right. I will add the attribute.
No need to add file-existence check here, because `IsReparsePointLikeSymlink` call did that already.

Design intention of the new LinkTarget() API was to rid of IsReparsePointLikeSymlink() :-)

(I don't ask to do this in the PR but we could review uses of IsReparsePointLikeSymlink())

By reviewing the code, it looks to me we can replace `IsReparsePointLikeSymlink(fileInfo)` with `fileInfo.LinkTarget` only if we don't treat `AppExecLink` as a symlink-like reparse point. But let's defer the discussion to it's own PR/issue.
So we wait public API for AppExecLink?

That could be an option. We will have conversation with the Windows App team again, so if they agreed to document the API, .NET can support AppExecLink, and we can get it for free. But for now, I'd say keep `IsReparsePointLikeSymlink`.

If AppExecLink will be public this can be addressed in `fileInfo.LinkTarget`. I think this was a design intention in the discussion with .Net Library team as well as removing `IsReparsePointLikeSymlink()`.
All that will have to wait until the AppExceLink API/struct is officially documented.
